finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If m_name contains a semicolon or other shell metacharacters, it could lead to command injection.
finding.assumptions: The code is running in an environment where the file name is interpreted by a shell, such as a script or a command line.

parsed.change_summary: Added a sanitize_filename function to remove shell metacharacters from m_name before appending it to log_file_name.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The sanitize_filename function removes shell metacharacters such as semicolons and other special characters from m_name before it is used to construct the log file name. This prevents the injected shell commands from being executed.
parsed.behavior_changes: The behavior of the code has changed in that it now sanitizes the file name to remove potentially harmful characters. Valid file names that do not contain these characters will still be processed as before.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The sink is std::ofstream::open, which does not invoke a shell or any command interpreter. The code merely concatenates strings to form a file name and passes that to open(). There is no path from the untrusted source m_name to a command execution primitive, so OS command injection is impossible. No additional checks are required.
